Hi Marta — thanks for sending the docs and welcome onboard.

Quick answers up front:
- If NovaPack is supplying services to Redwood Spain/UK where the place of supply is outside your local VAT registration, we typically apply reverse-charge (net invoice) for B2B services when we have a valid EU VAT+EORI proof.
- To make this smooth at PO time we need: legal entity on the supplier record, VAT number exactly as on the cert, country of registration, and a flag on the PO line "reverse_charge_candidate=true" so Finance routing can skip VAT remittance steps.

Can you confirm the exact entity/legal name to match the PO? Also please attach a signed W-8/W-9 equivalent if you have (for non-EU operations). Once we have the exact name + VAT id we can issue an exception template that your AP can include on invoices.

I copied Vivek (Tax Ops) and Laura (Procurement) to coordinate the PO-side exception and the template. Laura — can you review and advise the minimal PO field changes we need to accept net invoices under our SAP/ERP flow? Vivek — please confirm if the attached cert is sufficient for Redwood EU reverse-charge acceptance or if we need additional residency attestation.

Thanks Marta — I reviewed the certificate and EORI snapshot. Status: acceptable for reverse-charge for EU-to-EU B2B services, provided the invoice includes purchaser VAT (Redwood VAT id) and explicitly states "reverse charge applies".

Required evidence for our records: VAT certificate (supplied), proof of business registration (we can accept an excerpt from the Mercantile Registry), and a signed attestation that invoices will be submitted without local VAT under reverse-charge. If NovaPack can sign the short attestation (one page) we can store it in vendor master.

Laura — on the PO side we need an exception flow:
- PO header field: supplier_vat_id (text)
- PO line attribute: tax_handling = REVERSE_CHARGE or STANDARD
- When tax_handling = REVERSE_CHARGE, ERP must skip VAT tax calculation and set invoice validation to allow net amounts.
- A one-off PO exception ID should be stamped on the PO (e.g., EXC-YYYYMMDD-####) and referenced on the invoice.

I drafted a short PO-exception template and attached it to this thread for Laura/Neha to use: PO-exception-request-template.docx

Vivek
